2026 Market Update

Redpoint Ventures — Spring 2026

We're Living Through a Genuine Technological Revolution

  • AI infrastructure capex is tracking toward the largest technology investment wave in US history — projected to reach ~3.3% of GDP by 2030 on the bull case, rivaling the railroad and telecom buildoutsAI Software, Hardware & Infra (Bull): A dashed red line starting around 2021, showing a sharp upward trend to about 3.3% by 2030.
  • Hyperscaler CapEx surging from $309B in 2024 to $779B by 2027E — a 36% CAGR; Meta leads at 54% CAGRCY2024A $309B | CY2025E $498B | CY2026E $765B | CY2027E $779B. 2024A - 2027E CAGR: Overall: 36%, Meta: 54%, Google: 49%, Microsoft: 33%
  • This is not Dotcom 2.0: OpenAI and Anthropic each generating $20B+ ARR; >90% of data center capacity pre-committed; Nvidia EPS at ~$4.06 vs. Cisco's ~$0.37 at the 2000 peak
  • 1B+ monthly active users ~4 years post-ChatGPT vs. 70M internet users ~4 years post-Netscape

    • Awe-Inspiring Products Are Shipping Weekly

  • Jan '25 – DeepSeek R1: Crashed Nvidia stock ~17%; proved frontier-quality reasoning at a fraction of the cost
  • Apr '25 – Vibe Coding Goes Mainstream: Lovable, Replit, Cursor allow non-technical users to ship full apps; build cost drops from $500K/6 months (2015) to $50/6 hours (2026)
  • May '25 – AlphaFold 3: AI designs novel protein binders for new drugs; Jul '25 – IMO Gold: OpenAI & Google beat world's top mathematicians
  • Feb '26 – Waymo in 10 US Cities: 200M fully autonomous miles driven; Gemini 3.1 & Claude 4.6: Reasoning and agentic breakthroughs
  • Software developer demand is rising, not falling — Indeed job postings for software engineers recovered to 97% of Jan 2024 baseline by Jan 2026, outpacing total job postings (85%)JAN 26 | Indeed Job Posting for Software Engineers: 97 | Total Indeed Job Postings: 85

    • Agents Are Still Early — But the TAM Unlocks Are Enormous

  • We are largely at the Task Agent stage: AI executes discrete tasks end-to-end with human oversight, independent runtime of minutes
  • Each maturity level unlocks a dramatically larger addressable market:
  • Copilots → ~$0.5T US software spend
  • Task Agents → ~$1.2T (+$0.7T services automation)
  • Workflow Agents → ~$2.8T (+$1.6T operational payroll)
  • Autonomous → ~$6.1T+ (+$3.2T knowledge payroll)
  • Coding was the first domino: GitHub code YoY growth hit ~35% in 2025; new iOS apps up ~45% YoY; new websites up ~32% YoY — AI is expanding software creation, not contracting itThe growth rate starts at approximately 5% in 2021, fluctuates between -5% and 15% throughout 2022 and 2023, and experiences a sharp dip to -5% in early 2024. From 2024 onwards, there is a steep upward trend, reaching about 25% in 2025 and peaking at approximately 32% in 2026.
  • Mark Zuckerberg: "Every engineer is effectively gonna end up being more of like a tech lead in the future that has their own little army of engineering agents"

    • Software Stocks Are Down 20% YTD — But the Selloff Is Highly Uneven

  • Software is the worst-performing S&P 500 sector in 2026 YTD at -20%, vs. Energy at +32% and the S&P 500 at -5%Energy: 32%, S&P 500: (5%), Software: (20%)
  • Public SaaS median NTM revenue multiple has collapsed to 4.1x — near all-time lows, down from a peak of 22x in late 2020Current: 4.1x. The data line starts at approximately 4.5x in Dec-07, peaking at approximately 22x in late 2020. Following this peak, there is a sharp decline, with the multiple falling to around 5x by Dec-22 and stabilizing at a current value of 4.1x in Dec-25.
  • Not all SaaS is equal: Horizontal SaaS -35% LTM; Vertical SaaS +3%; Infrastructure +2% — the market is making a clear distinctionVertical SaaS: 3%, Infrastructure: 2%, Horizontal SaaS: -35%
  • Lowest-multiple names have the highest daily volatility (R² = 0.50) — the market is punishing uncertainty, not just weakness
  • Profitable growth commands a significant premium: >20% NTM growth companies trade at 8.1x vs. 2.9x for <10% growers

    • Why Horizontal SaaS Is Getting Hit Hardest

  • Vertical SaaS (+3%): Owns irreplaceable moats — proprietary industry data, compliance workflows, and years of process history. AI can augment but cannot displace without re-acquiring that data. Switching cost is existential, not cosmetic.
  • Infrastructure (+2%): AI is a direct tailwind. New AI workloads run on Snowflake, Datadog, MongoDB, Cloudflare. More AI deployment = more compute, data, and observability spend.
  • Horizontal SaaS (-35%): Accidentally optimized for replaceability — designed to serve every industry equally, integrating deeply with none. Without proprietary data or long process history, switching is easier. These products track who does what and when — exactly what AI handles well.
  • The real concern is terminal value, not near-term earnings: 85–95% of SaaS enterprise value comes from terminal value. A strong quarter moves <5% of value. Investors are pricing in near-zero long-term growth (implied terminal growth rate dropped from 4.7% to 1.1% in one quarter for a representative $100B company)3 MONTHS AGO: Market Cap $100B, Long-Term Growth Rate (implied) 4.7%. TODAY: Market Cap $73B, Long-Term Growth Rate (implied) 1.1%.

    • CIOs Are Actively Consolidating Vendors — Demand & Retention at Risk

  • 54% of CIOs are actively pursuing vendor consolidation; 45% of AI budgets are replacing existing software budgets; only 3% expect AI to lead to more vendors54% of CIOs are actively pursuing vendor consolidation. 45% of AI budgets are replacing existing software budgets. Only 3% of CIOs expect AI to lead to more vendors.
  • Top categories at risk of replacement (% of CIOs seriously considering switching in the last year): Customer Service Mgmt 26%, Finance Ops 21%, Project Mgmt 20%, Salesforce Automation 19%, HRIS 17%Customer Service Mgmt: 26%, Finance Ops: 21%, Project Mgmt: 20%, Salesforce Automation: 19%, HRIS: 17%
  • Pricing model shift underway: 46% of CIOs expect usage/outcome-based pricing to become more common; 35% expect flat subscriptions to declineUsage or Outcome Based: Will become more common 46%. Flat subscription: Will decline 35%.
  • AI is the #1 driver of software spend increases — 58% of CIOs cite AI feature additions as a key driver, the highest of any category

    • AI-Native Companies Are Growing at an Unprecedented Pace

  • OpenAI: $25B current revenue run-rate, projecting massive growth through 2028E; Anthropic: $19B current run-rateBar chart showing OpenAI Total Revenue Projections from 2024 to 2028E. The chart shows a significant increase in revenue over the five-year period, with a current revenue run-rate of $25B.
  • AI-native companies are achieving dramatically higher ARR/FTE ratios than traditional SaaS — a structural efficiency advantage that compounds over time
  • VC funding is nearly 100% AI-native by Q1 2026 (98% AI vs. 2% non-AI), up from ~35% in Q1 2020Q1 2026: AI-Native 98%, Non-AI 2%
  • VC dollars are concentrating: top 20 deals captured 44% of all enterprise software VC funding in 2025, up from just 8% in 20202020: 8%, 2021: 6%, 2022: 7%, 2023: 23%, 2024: 31%, 2025: 44%
  • Model Labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI) represent only 3% of deal count but capture 67% of dollars raised and 66% of enterprise value

    • Private Market Valuations Are Surging — Rounds Are Closing Faster

  • Median days between fundraising rounds has fallen sharply since mid-2023, reaching multi-year lows by early 2026 — the best companies are not waitingLine chart showing the median days between fundraising rounds from July 2023 to March 2026. The line shows a general downward trend, indicating that fundraising rounds are happening faster over time.
  • Seed valuations spiked to ~$60M median post-money by Q1 2026 (from ~$20M in Q1 2024); Series A to ~$150M; Series B to ~$480M; Series C to ~$1BSeed: spikes to nearly $60M by Q1'26 YTD. Series A: rises to approximately $150M by Q1'26 YTD. Series B: rises to $500M by Q4'25, slightly declines to approximately $480M by Q1'26 YTD. Series C: remains flat at approximately $1000M by Q1'26 YTD.
  • Late-stage private markets have become the new public markets: 24 private deals >$1B in 2025 vs. only 7 IPOs; 86% of US companies with $100M+ revenue are now private2025: Private Deals 24, IPOs 7. 86% are Private.
  • Historical pattern: companies founded 4–6 years after a major platform shift (i.e., 2026–2027 for AI) have historically been the biggest value creators — this is the "historical sweet spot"

    • What This Means for Your Company Right Now

  • Prove your moat is real: Investors and CIOs are asking the same question — does your product own irreplaceable data, workflow, or compliance? If not, articulate your switching cost clearly.
  • Rethink pricing before your customers do: Usage/outcome-based models are winning. 35% of CIOs expect flat subscriptions to decline. Get ahead of this shift proactively.
  • AI is a feature AND a threat: 58% of CIOs cite AI additions as the top driver of software spend increases — but 45% of AI budgets are replacing existing software. You need to be on the right side of both trends.
  • Fundraising windows are compressing: Rounds are closing faster, valuations are up sharply, but capital is concentrating in fewer deals. If you're raising, move with urgency — the best terms go to the fastest movers.
  • 2026–2027 is the historical sweet spot: Every major platform shift (Internet, Mobile, Cloud) produced its biggest winners from companies founded 4–6 years in. We are in that window now for AI.

    • Sources

  • Redpoint Ventures — 2026 Market Update (Spring 2026)
variables.instructions: Audience: portfolio company founders/operators. Tone: consultant — dense, information-rich cards (~200–300 words per card), each card 3–4+ bullets with specific data, metrics, and structured arguments; hard limit 320 words per card. Produce a 10‑slide market update using the provided outline; reuse strongest source visuals/charts from the PDF where they support the point; suggest charts/diagrams on slides with data. Emphasize actionable implications for founders (hiring/pricing/contracting/focus), include CIO survey metrics, public/private market moves, AI capex context, agent maturity/TAM, and clear top takeaways. Keep layout polished and presentation-ready.
